title: Streamline hetero-device fallbacks and CUDA API surface refactor
creator: Amit Kapoor
description: Refactor the CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS dependency surface and implement a lightweight heterogenous-device fallback layer to reduce probe latency, minimize symbol collisions, and provide deterministic safe fallbacks for mixed-GPU fleets. This ticket consolidates work to: (1) replace ad-hoc plugin probing with a timeboxed nonblocking probe, (2) extract a minimal CUTLASS shim for quantized kernels to avoid full CUTLASS symbol pulls, and (3) expose a small CUDA ABI facade used by runtime hot path to decouple driver-version-sensitive code paths.
acceptance_criteria: Nonblocking device probe completes or exits within 50ms on boot across tested instance types (A100, V100, T4)
Fallback policy returns verified scalar kernel variant or CPU fallback without raising user-visible error when kernel symbol mismatch detected
Integration tests updated to exercise new CUDA ABI facade and pass in CI matrix for cuda-11.8, cuda-12.1, cuda-12.3
PRs merging with end-to-end benchmark showing <=5% median latency regression and <=10% p95 regression vs baseline for long-sequence Llama-style workloads
Canary rollout automation updated: 5% nodes with runtime-2.4-canary, automatic rollback if kernel-load-failure-rate > 0.3% in 30m window
tasks: Design lightweight CUTLASS shim for int8/int4 matmul and test against quantized models
Implement nonblocking probe with adaptive backoff and telemetry (timebox 50ms)
Introduce cuda_abi_facade.h and move driver-sensitive queries behind facade
Add CI cross-build matrix entries for targeted CUDA versions and Triton plugin permutations
Create migration guide for Dedicated and Private deployment operators
Instrument runtime to emit kernel-load result metrics and add Grafana dashboard panel

notes: Rationale: Past kernel-compat patches pulled full CUTLASS and Triton symbols resulting in linker bloat and unpredictable startup latencies. A minimal shim plus a facade isolates the runtime hot path from driver-specific logic.
Tradeoffs: Increased maintenance burden for shim ABI but significantly lowers risk of runtime-wide symbol conflicts and reduces image size when only quantized kernels are required.

Rollback plan: If canary shows regressions, toggle runtime flag 'gpu_fallback_policy=v1' to revert to legacy probing and redeploy; emergency rollback playbook documented in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Runtime+Rollback+Playbook
